en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Gabled Hall.
Now at that time, the Venerable Kappitaka, the preceptor of the Venerable Upāli, was dwelling in a charnel ground.
At that time, the senior nun among the group of six bhikkhunīs had passed away.
The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having carried out that nun and cremated her not far from the Venerable Kappitaka’s dwelling, erected a stupa and went there to weep at that stupa.
Then the Venerable Kappita, distressed by that noise, broke up that stupa and scattered it.
The group-of-six bhikkhunīs thought, "This Kappita has destroyed our noble lady's stupa; come now, let us kill him! and they consulted together.
A certain bhikkhunī reported this matter to the Venerable Upāli.
The Venerable Upāli reported this matter to the Venerable Kappita.
Then the Venerable Kappita, having gone out from the monastery, remained hidden.
Then the group-of-six bhikkhunīs went to the dwelling of the venerable Kappita;
having arrived, they had the venerable Kappita’s dwelling covered over with stones and clods of earth, and departed, thinking, “Kappita is dead.
Then, at the end of that night, in the morning, the venerable Kappita dressed himself, took his bowl and robe, and entered Vesālī for alms.
The group-of-six bhikkhunīs saw the venerable Kappitaka walking for alms;
having seen him, they said:
"Kappitaka is alive! Who could have leaked our secret to him?"
The group-of-six bhikkhunīs heard:
"It seems that the venerable Upāli has gathered our secret spells.
They reviled the venerable Upāli.
“How can this wearer of the saffron robe, a mere cleaner of filth and of low birth, ever master our mantras?
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the bhikkhunīs of the group-of-six insult the noble Upāli?”... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs are reviling Upāli?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, could the group-of-six bhikkhunīs revile Upāli?

This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence... And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should revile a male lay follower, there is an offense of expiation."* *The full rule includes the context of the specific case involving Upāli and the stipulation regarding the nature of the reviling.*
“Whatever nun, however, should revile or abuse a monk, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"A bhikkhunī."
"An ordained person.
"Should revile" means:
either she reviles with the ten grounds for reviling, or with any one of them; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Or reviles":
she instills fear; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one addresses insults or reviles another who is ordained, perceiving them as ordained, there is an offense of expiation.
If she reviles or abuses one who is fully ordained while being in doubt [about their status], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she reviles or abuses one who is fully ordained while perceiving them as not fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation.
If she reviles or abuses one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If [the person] is not ordained, but one perceives them as ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If [the person] is not ordained, but one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If [the person] is not ordained, and one perceives them as not ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if it is for the sake of the welfare [of others],
or for the sake of the Dhamma.
[It is not an offense] for one who has instruction as her primary concern,
for one who is insane,
or for one who is a first-time offender.
The second training rule is finished.
